topic: Newton's method for nonlinear spring equilibrium in second-year mechanical engineering

entry_point.discipline_context: Mechanical engineers often use nonlinear force-displacement laws to model springs, linkages, and compliant structures.
entry_point.rationale: Starting from a spring equilibrium problem makes the root-finding target concrete before the Newton update is introduced.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: The spring analogy helps with intuition, but the numerical method is the same root-finding procedure used for any differentiable nonlinear equation.

chapter_sequence.title: From a nonlinear spring to a root-finding problem
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce equilibrium as a force-balance equation and define the root of interest.

chapter_sequence.title: Deriving Newton's step from a tangent line
chapter_sequence.purpose: Show how a local linear approximation produces the Newton iteration for the spring problem.

chapter_sequence.title: When the method is locally reliable
chapter_sequence.purpose: State the simple-root condition and the local quadratic convergence result.

chapter_sequence.title: Stopping criteria and practical checks
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain step tests, residual tests, derivative thresholds, and iteration limits.

chapter_sequence.title: Why Newton can fail and how damping helps
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain the main failure boundaries and the purpose of damping.

chapter_sequence.title: Python implementation and exercises
chapter_sequence.purpose: Connect the mathematics to a short Python implementation and provide exercises that reinforce the main ideas.

implementation_strategy: Use one compact spring example and a short Python function so the code directly mirrors the force-balance residual and the Newton update.
assessment_strategy: Provide six exercises that test derivation, interpretation, stopping criteria, damping choice, and simple implementation behaviour.
